title: Entropy upper bound on Hamming balls
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with at least two symbols, write $q = \abs{\alpha}$ for its size, and let $n$ be a natural number. Fix a real number $p$ with $0 < p \le 1 - 1/q$, and let
\[
H_q(p) \;=\; p\log_q(q-1) - p\log_q p - (1-p)\log_q(1-p)
\]
be the $q$-ary entropy function. Then for every codeword $c \in \alpha^n$, the Hamming ball of radius $\lfloor np\rfloor$ about $c$, namely $B_{\lfloor np\rfloor}(c) = \{c' \in \alpha^n : d(c',c) \le \lfloor np\rfloor\}$, satisfies
\[
\abs{B_{\lfloor np\rfloor}(c)} \;\le\; q^{\,H_q(p)\,n}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: alphabet is finite with at least two symbols (nontrivial)
q equals the size of the alphabet
n a natural number, codewords of length n
